payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. On 8 September in the GHL Dev group Ahmed reported that all Full Smile tasks are complete with one item left pending approval to make it live, asked for a review and a comment on Monday, and then asked separately for approval on the Full Smile workflows so he can enable those as well. Sohib said he would check at 8AM CST on 9 September. This item is where that approval belongs, since it is the item that specifies the workflows and it has sat at For Review since 4 August.
  • What is waiting for a decision. This item covers the instant form reply, the two stage appointment confirmation SMS with C and X reply logic, the Open Dental status writeback where green means confirmed and yellow means reminder sent, the review request trigger on the Request Review pipeline stage, and Google and LSA inbound calls creating Opportunities rather than only contacts. Confirm which of those are built and which one is the single outstanding approval, because Ahmed's message says one pending item and this item lists five deliverables.
  • Deliverable one, review and approve or reject, in writing on this item. Ahmed is blocked on a yes or no and will not enable anything until he gets it. An approval given only in WhatsApp leaves the board showing For Review indefinitely, which is exactly the state this item has been in for five weeks.
  • Deliverable two, enable and prove each workflow. Once approved, enable the workflows and post a test result per workflow: a test form submission returning the instant reply, a test appointment producing the two day and two hour reminders with C and X both handled, a pipeline move firing the review request, and a test call from Google or LSA landing as an Opportunity.
  • Deliverable three, tell the client. Full Smile are mid renewal conversation and were told the conversion gap is where the work is going. Automated reminders and instant replies are that work, so the fact they are live belongs in the next client message.
  • Dependencies and constraints. Blocked on internal approval only, nothing external. Do not enable the appointment reminders before confirming the A2P and messaging position on this account, because Full Smile also have an open messaging block over a payment method on the GoHighLevel location, and enabling automated SMS into an account that cannot send produces silent failures rather than errors.
  • done = the outstanding workflow is approved or rejected in writing here, every approved workflow is enabled with a passing test result posted per workflow, and the client has been told what is now live.

items.title: Intake Speed Audit
items.note: Section 19 audit covered Full Smile groups on all four boards. Patient Workflows 12714615372 covers building the follow up automations but nothing measures the existing funnel, the Reports item 12175493646 and its subitems are per platform ad reporting rather than intake, and Budget Shift 12766744655 and the Meta Campaign Review 12906933112 are media decisions. Nothing owns the intake measurement, so drafted as a new CRM item. Routed to CRM rather than Web and SEO because the data lives in GoHighLevel pipelines and call logs, matching how the equivalent Maadi Law intake work was routed. Kept separate from fullsmile-booked-showed-sync per the merge counter rule. Section 19b returned no match.

payload.updateBody:
Salam,

  • Context. In his 8 September message to Full Smile, Sohib laid out the numbers the account is being judged on: Meta put 132 leads in front of the practice last month and 6 became patients. The practice paid for all 132, so his argument to the client was that closing the conversion gap is cheaper than adding budget. He then committed to the practice that he is auditing how fast those leads get called back and where they drop off, and said that is usually where most of the 132 goes. This item is that audit. It is a commitment already made to a client who is deciding whether to keep spending.
  • Deliverable one, measure speed to first contact. For every one of last month's Meta leads, pull the gap between lead creation and the first genuine outbound contact attempt, by call and by text separately. Post the median and, more importantly, the share contacted within five minutes, within one hour, on the same day, and never. The never bucket is the one that matters.
  • Deliverable two, find where they stop. Map the 132 through the pipeline stage by stage and post the count surviving each step: contacted, reached a human, appointment booked, appointment showed, became a patient. Six patients out of 132 means roughly 126 stopped somewhere specific, and the whole point of this is to name that step rather than describe the funnel generally.
  • Deliverable three, separate bad leads from bad follow up. Split the drop off into leads never contacted, leads contacted and unreachable, leads reached and not booked, and leads booked and no show. Those four have completely different fixes and only the first two are within Flow's control.
  • Deliverable four, one recommendation. Turn the finding into a single named change with an expected effect on monthly new patients. Sohib has already told the client the target is 9 percent conversion, roughly 21 patients a month on the same spend, bringing cost per patient from $411 down towards $293, so the recommendation has to be measured against that number and not a generic improvement.
  • Dependencies and constraints. No client dependency, all of this is in the GoHighLevel account already. Do not mix this with the Open Dental booked and showed integration on the Booked Showed Sync item, which is a build and will not land in time for this reply. Use whatever booking data exists today, even if imperfect, and say which parts are estimated. Findings feed the August Account Review reply, so post the numbers here rather than only summarising them to the client.
  • done = a written breakdown of last month's 132 Meta leads is posted on this item showing time to first contact, the survival count at each pipeline stage, the four way split of why leads dropped, and one named recommendation with its expected effect on monthly new patient count.

@Ahmed Memon @Ali Shaheer
